1. **Outside view.** The Economist/YouGov tracker started Trump's second term around 49–50% approve (late Jan/early Feb 2025), slid into the low 40s by spring 2025, and settled into a fairly narrow 38–41% band through the second half of 2025, with net approval around –15 to –19. Week-to-week movement in this series is small: typical change between adjacent waves is about 1 point, with an sd of roughly 1.5 points (design effect plus true drift). The series is "sticky" — Trump-era approval has historically had very low variance because partisanship is locked in. A naive extrapolation from a late-2025 level near 39% with a mild continuing downward drift over three quarters would put a Sept 2026 wave around 38–40%.

2. **Inside view.** The release is fielded the weekend of ~Aug 29–31, 2026 and published Sept 1–2. Specifics I can reason about without data: (a) It is a midterm election year, and the out-party enthusiasm environment plus affordability/cost-of-living salience has been the main drag on this number — worth maybe –0.5 to –1 relative to late 2025. (b) Late-August fielding means low news salience (recess, summer), which historically neither helps nor hurts much (~0). (c) There is a floor effect: this tracker rarely dips below ~36 because ~85–90% GOP approval plus a slice of independents mechanically supports high-30s. (d) There is also a real possibility of partial consolidation/recovery if inflation cooled — worth +1 to +2 in an upside branch. Net: I nudge slightly below the 2025 late-year level, to ~38.8.

3. **Pre-mortem.** The most likely way I'm badly wrong is a regime change in the level during the ~9 months I can't observe — e.g., a recession, a major scandal, or a foreign-policy crisis pushing this into the low-to-mid 30s, or conversely a rally/economic improvement putting it back at 43–44. A secondary failure mode is a YouGov weighting/methodology change (they've adjusted party-ID targets before) shifting the level by 1–2 points. Correction: widen the sd well beyond the 1.5-point week-to-week noise, and keep the distribution roughly symmetric but with slightly more room on the downside.

4. **Calibrate.** Week-to-week sd is ~1.5, but level uncertainty over an unobserved 9-month gap dominates. An sd of ~3 points means two-thirds of the mass falls in roughly 36–42, which matches the plausible range given the 2025 trajectory and the empirical floor/ceiling of this series.
